notes:
Account summary: Inkling CodeWorks builds an IDE copilot (VS Code + JetBrains) used internally by ~350 engineers. Primary ask: predictable Dedicated capacity to cover peak developer hours and burst events (hack days). They need sub-100ms streaming token delivery for completions in the editor and model/version pinning for reproducible suggestion behavior. Strong preference for open-models & Redwood-verified variants.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-20: Intro call (AE) — initial fit: devtools optimization, cost sensitivity but willing to commit for predictable UX.
- 2026-02-24: SE demo — live streaming demo with 95th pct latency test; customer asked about <80ms 95p target for 8-token streaming chunks. (See ff_20260302_3472 transcript)
- 2026-02-28: Sent draft Dedicated sizing and pricing (drive://Inkling/Redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1).
- 2026-03-05: Security sync with Okta/SAML team; asked for KMS + 1yr audit log retention (ff_20260305_3511).
- 2026-03-08: Procurement questionnaire returned with legal and network egress concerns. Jira ticket INF-9821 opened for network config clarifications.

Use-case & requirements (short):
- Workload: IDE copilot + background code indexing for completions and embeddings-based repo search. Real-time streaming is critical.
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 80ms for short completions in editor (first-token stream latency <50ms desirable).
- Throughput: predictable baseline 1.5k-2k requests/hour during working hours (10:00-12:00 & 18:00-20:00 ET). Peak bursts up to 6k req/hr during hack days/weekly releases.
- Model requirements: pin to a verified model build (v1.3) with deterministic fallback to v1.2 (lower-cost) on capacity constraints. Need per-route model pinning and rollout policy controls.
- Cost sensitivity: high for token-heavy batch jobs (indexing) but will accept premium for editor latency guarantees. Looking for Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) to limit ARR.
- Security/compliance: Okta SSO (SAML), KMS for customer-managed keys, audit logging for 12 months, US data residency for customer data.

POC plan (agreed):
1) Week 0: Network and security questionnaire — customer to provide firewall rules and NAT/GW details. (blocked by network-egress-policy)
2) Week 1: Dedicated trial cluster sized for 2x baseline throughput + burst config; SE to deliver config doc and SLOs. (SE: Liam O'Connor)
3) Week 2: Integrate VS Code extension streaming with Redwood Dedicated endpoints; measure 95/99 latencies, token usage, and failure modes. Logging + audit events validated.
4) Week 3: Cost run and final sizing + procurement sign-off. Target: production go-live within 8 weeks after POC.

Quotes / call notes:
- "We can't tolerate visible lag in autocompletions — developer flow collapses." — Head of Engineering
- "If you can guarantee the latency profile and model pinning, procurement will push for a quarterly commit." — EngOps

Open questions / blockers:
- Procurement asks for deeper TCO (breakdown of reserved vs burst pricing). AE to provide.
- Network egress: customer uses strict outbound rules; needs exact CIDR list for Dedicated instances (INF-9870).
- Security: confirm KMS key rollover process and audit log export cadence (SEC-410).

Next actions (owners):
- AE (Maya): deliver TCO + updated pricing with burst policy examples by 2026-03-14.
- SE (Liam): produce Dedicated sizing + deployment runbook; schedule infra deep-dive w/ customer network team.
- CSM (Priya): prep onboarding checklist & retention controls once contract signed.

Stubs / linked artifacts: drive://Inkling/Redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1, drive://Inkling/POC-runbook, ff_20260302_3472, thread:17a9c3b2, INF-9821.

Notes tone: choppy, CRM-style actions + bullets. Customer enthusiastic about committing if latency & model pinning guaranteed.
